title: Training-crawler policy is stated
question: Has the site made a decision about AI training crawlers, whatever it is?
method: Pass when robots.txt states a training decision in any form: a group for the shared token __usage_ai-training (the IETF draft Google, Microsoft and OpenAI have committed to), groups naming the documented training crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, meta-externalagent, Amazonbot, CCBot, Bytespider, MistralAI-Training), or a Content-Signal or Content-Usage line that sets ai-train or train-ai. Allowing and disallowing count the same: blocking training is a licensing decision and never loses points. Warn when nothing is stated. The evidence lists the effective verdict per token.

spec.title: draft-kelley-aipref-training-preference-signal: a shared robots.txt token for AI training preferences
Google Search Central: a robots.txt control for AI training

title: Search and assistant crawlers may read product pages
question: Do the crawlers that feed AI answers get in?
method: Evaluate robots.txt against a sampled product path (the home page when none) for the crawlers that build the indexes behind AI answers: Googlebot and Bingbot (Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, Microsoft Copilot and ChatGPT search, Claude search via Brave), Applebot, Storebot-Google, OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Amzn-SearchBot, DuckAssistBot, MistralAI-Index and meta-webindexer. Fail when Googlebot or Bingbot is disallowed or when two or more of the others are; warn when exactly one is; pass otherwise. The evidence shows the effective rule per crawler.

title: Usage-preference signals parse
question: Are the machine-readable usage preferences the site declares well-formed?
method: Informational. Collect every usage-preference signal found: Content-Signal lines in robots.txt, Content-Usage rules in robots.txt and the Content-Usage response header, an RSL License line in robots.txt or a Link relation of type application/rsl+xml, and TDM reservations (/.well-known/tdmrep.json, tdm-reservation header or meta tag). Pass when every signal present is syntactically valid, or when none is declared; warn when one is malformed. The three vocabularies share no tokens and are never mapped onto each other, and no crawler operator documents honouring Content-Signal, so this is reported and never scored.

spec.title: draft-ietf-aipref-attach: attaching AI usage preferences via robots.txt and HTTP
TDM Reservation Protocol (W3C Community Group Report)

title: No block or challenge on an honest fetch
question: Does an agent that identifies itself truthfully get the pages?
method: Inspect the responses the scan already made with its own user agent (AgenticReadinessScanner, with a documentation URL): the home page, the sampled product pages, the policy pages and robots.txt. Fail when any answered 402, 403, 429 or 451, carried a bot-management challenge marker (the cf-mitigated: challenge header, or a challenge page served as 200), or was answered by an access-denied page. Warn when a page redirected to a consent or geographic interstitial instead of its content. The scanner never impersonates another agent, so what it meets is what any unverified agent meets; crawlers verified by published IP ranges or signatures may be treated differently, which the message says.

spec.title: Cloudflare: detecting a challenge page response

title: User-triggered fetchers are not disallowed
question: When a person asks an assistant about this site, may the assistant fetch the page?
method: Evaluate robots.txt against the sampled product path for the fetchers assistants use at the moment a person asks: ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, Perplexity-User, Google-Agent, meta-externalfetcher, Amzn-User and MistralAI-User. Fail when any is disallowed. Most operators document that these fetch regardless of robots.txt because a person requested the page (Anthropic honours it), so a Disallow mostly records intent; the weight is low for that reason.

title: No directives that keep product pages out of AI answers
question: Do page-level directives withdraw the product from AI answers?
method: Read meta robots, meta bingbot and X-Robots-Tag on sampled product pages and look for data-nosnippet around the main content. Fail on noindex. Warn on nosnippet or max-snippet:0 (Google says these also exclude the page from AI Overviews and AI Mode), on a data-nosnippet attribute wrapping the main content, on Bing noarchive, nocache or ai-grounding:disallow (Copilot answers), and on isAccessibleForFree:false in the page JSON-LD (Apple Intelligence). noai and noimageai are recorded as a declared preference that no major crawler documents honouring, not as a restriction.
